title: Blocksy vs Kadence
description: A documentation-led comparison of Blocksy’s Customizer-first controls and Kadence’s visual header, footer, and global design workflow.
metaDescription: A transparently scoped Blocksy versus Kadence WordPress comparison from KreativWP.
comparisonAreas: Customizer-first controls versus visual header and footer builders
Global color, typography, and layout settings
Documented ecommerce and page-level layout workflow
Same-content performance, accessibility, and support tests still required
takeaway: Blocksy is a sensible research path for site builders who prefer many presentation controls in a familiar Customizer workflow. Kadence deserves attention when visual header, footer, and global-design controls are central to the build.

decisionGuide.chooseLeft: a Customizer-led workflow and page-level layout overrides are familiar to the person maintaining the site.
decisionGuide.chooseRight: the team wants visual header and footer control alongside centrally managed palette, typography, and layout settings.
decisionGuide.verify: Recreate your navigation, one product or landing page, and the mobile states before deciding. Confirm the feature and plan boundaries for your use case.

rows.label: Everyday editing
rows.left: Classic theme controls in the Customizer, including global presentation and header/footer building.
rows.right: Classic theme with header/footer building and global palette, typography, and layout controls.

rows.label: Free versus paid
rows.left: Free theme; Companion and Pro extend the ecosystem. Check the exact feature and edition.
rows.right: Free theme; Pro, blocks, and other packages extend the ecosystem. Theme and block-plugin licenses are distinct.

rows.label: Content editor
rows.left: Supports WordPress blocks and documented page-builder integrations; it is not a full-site-editing block theme.
rows.right: Supports blocks within its theme layout system; Kadence Blocks is a separate plugin, not a requirement for core blocks.

rows.label: Store considerations
rows.left: Documented WooCommerce controls; advanced extensions have edition limits.
rows.right: Documented WooCommerce styling and layout controls; confirm Pro boundaries for the required store features.

migration: Try the same desktop and phone header in both. Theme-specific header elements, palettes, and Customizer settings do not transfer automatically. The profile tests cover free themes and core blocks—not a WooCommerce checkout or premium extension migration.
